summary: Red Top's 1952 L-4 cab replaced a 1928 D-6 cupola; abandoned in the 1970s, restored 1996-97, and reported volunteer-staffed in summer.

facts.design: 10-foot treated timber tower with an L-4 wooden cab and catwalk

staffing.status: volunteer-staffed in summer (sources conflict on the 2017 status)

access.note: NHLR calls it a public information site; the interior is visible when the lookout is open, and the trail is about 1.5 miles round trip.

visit.trail_note: Trailhead reached via Forest Roads 9738 and 9702 from Highway 97; about 1.5 miles round trip with about 350 ft of gain.

events.note: Millmade Construction shipped two standard lookout houses to the Forest Service; one reportedly went to Red Top
First cabin on the site (TrailChick); Willhite says the cupola cabin's build date is unclear, possibly as late as 1924
Earlier cabin replaced by a D-6 cupola ground house
Lightning struck the summit several times and hit the lookout at least twice (November 1929)
Present 10-foot timber tower with L-4 cab built; replaced the D-6 cupola
Restored 1996 and 1997 by the Cle Elum Ranger District and the Friends of Red Top Mountain
Registered August 6, 1997 as US 225, WA 28; summit dedication August 26, 1997

resolved_conflicts.explanation: Sources give 1918 (shipment, possible Red Top), 1924 (first cabin), 1928 (D-6 cupola) and 1952 (present L-4 tower). The brief's 1952 date is for the present structure; the story reports the earlier dates as well.
NHLR gives a registration date of August 6, 1997; TrailChick describes a summit party on August 26, 1997 to celebrate the register listing. Both are kept, since they are different events.
NHLR gives the summit at 5,168 ft (1,575 m); TrailChick gives 5,361 ft. The record keeps the NHLR figure.
Willhite says volunteers staff it in summer. TrailChick's 2017 post says it used to be staffed and also that it is now staffed in summers. The story reports this as inconsistent.

sources.title: Red Top Lookout (Red Top Mountain Lookout)

notes_for_editor: Dates are the hardest part of this record. The 1918 shipment is quoted from a 1918 Oregonian item reprinted on Washington Lookouts; that page calls the destination Red Mountain, and Willhite says the house ended up at Red Top, so the link is plausible but not certain. The 1952 L-4 cab is consistent across four sources. The abandonment year is not given beyond the 1970s, so no event was recorded for it. Sources do not agree on whether volunteers staffed the lookout in 2017; the story says so rather than choosing. The brief's record (1952 built, 1997 registered) is consistent with the evidence, so no corrections were proposed. The WTA page describes the trail as an easy hike; the record does not need it. Willhite Web and TrailChick are personal trip-report sites, used for dates and access details only. The Washington Lookouts page is a secondary compilation; the 1918 and 1926 items are quoted from it. Several local pages list the same site under the name Red Top Mountain.
